questions.q: Now that analytics.fact_orders is validated, why doesn't Redshift becoming the primary path retire Athena entirely?
options: Athena is required to refresh the Glue Catalog
Redshift cannot run SELECT statements at all
A full COPY load is overkill for a one-off question nobody will repeat, so a lighter query path still has real value
Athena is actually faster than Redshift for every query
questions.explain: Loading an entire month into the warehouse just to answer a question once is wasted work; Spectrum/Athena stay useful for that case.

questions.q: What does Redshift Spectrum let you do?
options: Automatically load all S3 data into Redshift tables on a schedule
Convert CSV files into Parquet automatically
Replace the need for an IAM role entirely
Query data sitting in S3 directly through the Glue Catalog, without loading it into a Redshift table first
questions.explain: Spectrum queries the external catalog table in place, reading from S3 directly rather than requiring a load.

questions.q: What does the CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA statement in this lesson point the new spectrum schema at?
options: The existing northfield_catalog Glue database, the same one the crawler and ETL job's sink already populate
The raw S3 zone only, bypassing the curated zone
The analytics schema inside Redshift
A brand-new, empty Glue database created just for Spectrum
questions.explain: CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA ... FROM DATA CATALOG DATABASE 'northfield_catalog' reuses the catalog database that already exists.

questions.q: Why does the CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA statement reuse northfield-redshift-copy-role rather than a different role?
options: Spectrum needs the same kind of S3 read access that a COPY load does
Redshift Spectrum does not support IAM roles
IAM roles can only be used once per AWS account
That role is required specifically for creating Glue databases
questions.explain: Spectrum reads from S3 just like COPY does, so it reuses the same role that already grants that read access.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which situation calls for loading data into analytics.fact_orders rather than querying spectrum.northfield_orders_curated directly?
options: Any question that only needs a single partition's data
A quick sanity check against the raw, uncleaned data
A one-off question nobody is likely to ask again
A recurring, trusted monthly report that will be run and relied on repeatedly
questions.explain: A recurring, trusted report is exactly the repeat, join-heavy workload the warehouse load is built for.
